doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

chapter: Photographs of the Creole Fiesta and family
title: Reel 3 opening: pictures of grandchildren as mademoiselles and queens
summary: Allen opens the third reel; Edna names her granddaughters in Fiesta photographs, including Barbara Ann as queen to her grandfather king.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Interview openings: names, dates and tape setup

blocks.x: That's where they all had the mademoiselles. Let me say this is Rio 3, and we're interviewing Mrs. and Mrs. A.C. Senegal, May the 24th, 1862. See, we've seen these pictures of your grandchildren here. We talked about that just on the end of the last Rio. And then you showed me the picture of the boy in the moment here too. Yeah.

Uh-huh. Yeah, she wanted me to say the names of these on this picture? Yeah. This is my granddaughter, Sylvia Serena. She's now Mrs. Webb. And she's the first, she was the first mademoiselle Fiesta. And Barbara Ann, Senegal, granddaughter of Mrs. A.C. Senegal, Mrs. Senegal. And she was a queen when her grandfather was king. She was king, she was a queen. She was king, right? That was nice. That was nice. When he was king, she was his queen. And this is Jocelyn Marie's Romanian. She was maid to her cousin. No, no, one of your granddaughters. One of my granddaughters. She's in Pasadena, California now. So these are the three granddaughters. Now this is a picture of the board members. We have six here. Mrs. Leona B. Santavide. Mrs. Bernice Bozant. Mrs. Romagna de Masserier. Mrs. Edna Bibelet Serena Senegal, founder and president. Mrs. Vivian Yates, first vice president. And Mrs. Clara Mare, correspondent secretary. Mrs. C. Donnelly, you want to see these? Want to go through these?
